answer: A garden of agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit before it may transact, like a lantern that only lights after fuel is paid. The stake is slashed when peers attest misbehavior, so creating many fake identities in the meadow of the network costs real money per copy. An attacker must fund every sockpuppet separately, while honest agents earn their deposit back with good service, making a sybil flood unprofitable at scale.
